name: The Sea and Cake
label: Thrill Jockey
lede: A painter, a cartoonist, a photographer and Chicago's busiest drummer take their name from a Gastr del Sol song title they bent on purpose, then make the lightest-sounding records of the post-rock years.

eras.title: Out of Shrimp Boat and the Coctails
eras.text: Two Chicago bands wound down in the early 1990s: Shrimp Boat, with Sam Prekop and Eric Claridge, and The Coctails, with Archer Prewitt. The survivors found a drummer who was already in Tortoise.

years.h: Sam Prekop and Eric Claridge start Shrimp Boat in Chicago
years.p: With Ian Schneller, David Kroll and later Brad Wood, Shrimp Boat puts out seven releases on labels including Bar/None and Rough Trade before it ends in 1993.
years.xp:
Prekop sang and played guitar and bass; Claridge played drums and bass. The group's releases ran from Some Biscuit in 1988 through Cavale, with Speckly, Volume One and Duende in between, and a compilation, Something Grand, followed in 2004.

When the band ended, Schneller and Tom Jasek started Falstaff. Schneller later founded the guitar maker Specimen Products.

years.h: Archer Prewitt co-founds the Coctails
years.p: The Coctails leave Kansas City for Chicago after their 1989 debut, then make six albums in all before a last show on New Year's Eve 1995.

years.h: Prewitt colors Marvel comics and self-publishes Sof' Boy on the side
years.p: The mini-comics are his own. His day job is colorist for Marvel Comics, and in 1998 the Eisner Awards nominate him for Best Colorist.
years.xp:
The nomination was for his work on Sof' Boy and Friends #1, published in 1997. Kitchen Sink Press and Fantagraphics Books both later published the comic.

Prewitt also created a character called Funny Bunny and drew for Mome and Timothy McSweeney's Quarterly Concern.

years.h: Shrimp Boat dissolves, and the Sea and Cake takes its place
years.p: Prekop and Claridge recruit Prewitt and [[John McEntire|73e452bb-1f86-4dec-a2aa-a8b097fea4c6]], who is already drumming in Tortoise.

years.h: A Gastr del Sol song title, misread on purpose, becomes the name
years.p: Wikipedia calls it a "willful reinterpretation" of The C in Cake, from McEntire's earlier project [[Gastr del Sol|8f54d90b-f322-4e5d-a0fd-bdc960f2d20f]].

eras.title: A quick start on Thrill Jockey
eras.text: Thrill Jockey put out the first three Sea and Cake records in quick succession. Claridge painted the covers and Prekop took the photos, and by 1997 McEntire was building the songs in a computer.

years.src: Thrill Jockey: The Sea and Cake
years.h: The debut, The Sea and Cake, sets the template
years.p: Sam Prekop sings softly and half-sings over interlocking guitars, and McEntire's drumming stays light enough to pass for jazz.
years.xp: Thrill Jockey's own description of the band's sound, which this record fixes in place: "delicate, intertwining guitar patterns, syncopated rhythms, and airy melodies."

years.h: Prekop designs the sleeve of Tortoise's first album
years.p: The record is also on Thrill Jockey, and [[Tortoise|e0953daa-860f-4dc8-9f1a-b12587cdaf17]] and the Sea and Cake share McEntire for decades afterward.

years.h: Nassau, album two, opens a double-release year
years.p: It's the first of two Sea and Cake albums in 1995.

years.h: The Biz makes it two albums in one year
years.p: That's three records since 1994, all within about two years.

years.h: The Sea and Cake lends The Fontana to an AIDS benefit album
years.p: The song goes on Red Hot + Bothered, a Red Hot Organization compilation.

years.h: Lissy's Records presses Glad You're Right in 500 copies
years.p: The 7-inch carries Tiger Panther and Crimson Wing on the other side.

years.cap: Live at Silk City, Philadelphia, May 2, 1997
years.src: Wikipedia: The Sea and Cake · Wikipedia: John McEntire · Wikipedia: Archer Prewitt
years.h: McEntire runs Pro Tools for the first time on The Fawn
years.p: The fourth album adds drum machines and synthesizers to the jazz, samba and bossa nova. McEntire is an early Pro Tools user.
years.xp: The same year brought Two Gentlemen, a 12-inch of mostly remixes, and A Brief Historical Retrospective, a Japan-only compilation. Prewitt also released his first solo album, In the Sun.

eras.title: Side projects, and a Bowie cover
eras.text: Everyone had somewhere else to be. Prekop made a solo record with Jim O'Rourke, Prewitt kept releasing his own, and McEntire ran Soma and Tortoise. The band still came back for Oui and One Bedroom.

years.h: Sam Prekop makes a solo record, with Jim O'Rourke at the board
years.p: Sam Prekop is soft and Brazilian-leaning, with Josh Abrams, Chad Taylor and Archer Prewitt along.

years.h: Window Lights is a Hefty single, then a soundtrack cut
years.p: Hefty Records releases it with Setup for Bed on the other side, and it lands on the Reach the Rock soundtrack.

years.h: Oui arrives after three years of solo records
years.p: The fifth album is the band's first in three years, made after Prekop, Prewitt and McEntire each spent time on other work.

years.cap: Live at the Empty Bottle, Chicago, July 4, 2003
years.h: One Bedroom ends on a Bowie cover
years.p: Sound and Vision closes the sixth album, with John and Frank Navin singing along. It reaches 16 on Billboard's independent chart.
years.xp:
Recorded at McEntire's Soma Electronic Music Studios and released January 21, 2003, the album carries electric piano from Mikael Jorgensen of [[Wilco|9e53f84d-ef44-4c16-9677-5fd4d78cbd7d]] on two tracks. The band wrote everything except the Bowie song.

Pitchfork gave it 7.0. Metacritic's score is 79 out of 100.

years.h: The Glass EP rounds off the first decade
years.p: It's a CD EP, out the year before the band stops.

eras.title: Three years off, then a louder record
eras.text: The band stopped in 2004 and returned in 2007, recording in a Michigan studio. Four records followed in six years, each with Claridge's paintings or Prekop's photos on the cover.

years.cap: Back on stage three years later
years.h: The Sea and Cake stops after ten years and six albums
years.p: Prekop, Prewitt and McEntire keep busy with solo records, comics, Tortoise and production.

years.cap: Live at Richards on Richards, Vancouver, May 14, 2007
years.src: Wikipedia: Everybody (The Sea and Cake album)
yt: Parasol, in-store at Sound Fix Records, c. 2007
years.h: Three years off, then Everybody from a Michigan studio
years.p: Sessions at Key Club in Benton Harbor and at Soma in Chicago produce what PopMatters calls the most rock-based record the band has made.
years.xp:
Pitchfork's Jason Crock gave it 7.6, writing that the band "remain relevant simply by becoming more transparent." PopMatters' Michael Franco gave 6 out of 10 and said it "sounds modern, sophisticated, and ultra-cool." Exclaim!'s Vish Khanna called it "a mature yet adventurous effort."

Metacritic scored it 74 out of 100 from 24 reviews. It reached number 9 on Billboard's Heatseekers chart and 32 on the independent albums chart, and was released May 8, 2007.

years.h: A year after Everybody, Car Alarm
years.p: The eighth album is the second since the band's return from its break in 2004.

years.h: The Sea and Cake bootlegs itself, officially, at Chicago's Metro
years.p: Metro: The Official Bootleg Series, Volume 1 documents the band live at the club.

years.big: "uniquely inventive blend of lilting pop and obtuse art-rock"
years.h: Mojo sums up the band in one line on The Moonlight Butterfly
years.p: David Sheppard writes it in Mojo's July 2011 issue, reviewing the ninth album, a compact one.

years.h: Runner is the last record with Eric Claridge
years.p: The tenth album is the last to feature Claridge, the band's bassist and cover painter.

eras.title: Down to three
eras.text: Without Claridge, the band wrote as a trio for the first time. Doug McCombs of Tortoise came along on bass for shows.

years.src: Thrill Jockey: The Sea and Cake · Wikipedia: Doug McCombs
years.h: Eric Claridge is out, and the Sea and Cake writes as a trio
years.p: Any Day is the first album without Claridge. Sam Prekop's take on writing as a trio comes from Thrill Jockey's bio.
years.xp:
After Runner the three went their own ways: Prekop into modular synthesis and soundtracks, McEntire to Tortoise and production, Prewitt to cartooning. Prekop says the excitement came as soon as they started playing together.

Doug McCombs of [[Tortoise|e0953daa-860f-4dc8-9f1a-b12587cdaf17]] and [[Brokeback|e3fa3b7a-b883-4432-9152-ed0cf4d5c19c]] joins as touring bassist from May 2018. No public reason for Claridge's exit appears in the sources.

years.src: Thrill Jockey: The Sea and Cake
years.h: Any Day swaps synthesizers for stacked guitars and organs
years.p: Paul Von Mertens plays flute and clarinet and Nick Macri double bass behind Prekop's most vocal-centered songs. The Guardian: "elegantly disheveled, melodic jazz rock."
years.xp: Thrill Jockey says the record goes for organic instrumentation, with Prewitt's guitar effects supplying the textures and McEntire's drumming and mixing giving the minimal approach "a nimble shimmer." Von Mertens and Macri play on the title track.

years.h: Prekop and McEntire go modular on Sons Of
years.p: The two release a duo album built on modular synthesizers, Prekop's focus since Old Punch Card in 2010.
years.xp: His 2015 album The Republic pushed further into what Wikipedia calls the emotional possibilities of the modular synthesizer: nine tracks made for an art installation by David Hartt. Comma followed in 2020.
